segments.t: Exhausted after a sleepless night listening to Rodion cough and snore, Kostya corners Nastya in the morning and suggests it is time for their guest to return to the street. Outraged by Kostya's lack of compassion, Nastya declares that if Kostya kicks Rodion out, she will pack her bags and leave with him.
Я не знал об этом вашем семейном правиле.
Костя, ты слышал, как он кашлял всю ночь?
То я уйду вместе с ним.
Let's replay the exchange and look closely at each Russian phrase.
'Actually, I am not asleep.' Kostya anchors the line on 'actually', while 'sleep' completes the thought.
'I am right here.' Nastya brings out the contrast between 'I' and 'already' in a few short words. Rodion answers right away.
'I beg your pardon, Konstantin.' The meaning hinges on 'beg' working together with 'Konstantin' in spoken Russian.
Я не знал об этом вашем семейном правиле.
'I did not know about that family rule of yours.' The '-l' ending on the verb meaning 'knew' places the action in the masculine past tense.
'Well then.' Nastya anchors the line on 'come on', while 'what' completes the thought. Rodion answers right away.
'Do you not think.' The meaning hinges on 'and' working together with 'it seems' in spoken Russian.
'That it is time for him to head back out to the street?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'to him' before landing on 'street'.
Костя, ты слышал, как он кашлял всю ночь?
'Kostya, did you hear how he was coughing all night long?' Notice how Russian expresses 'Kostya' and 'night' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Rodion answers right away.
'I heard him, Nastya.' The meaning hinges on 'heard' working together with 'Nastya' in spoken Russian.
'I cannot take this anymore.' Kostya anchors the line on 'I', while 'can' completes the thought.
'Then I will leave too.' The meaning hinges on 'then' working together with 'will leave' in spoken Russian. Rodion answers right away.
'Nastya, what kind of principle is that?' The grammar packs 'Nastya' and 'principles' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
То я уйду вместе с ним.
'Then I will walk out right along with him.' Kostya anchors the line on 'then', while 'him' completes the thought. Let's hear the complete conversation once more.
